=== version ===
susi <VERSION>

=== susi ===
susi: RSI swarm AI OS for hosting, provisioning, and managing local and cloud AI — GAWD, GEMI & GMCP

Usage: susi [INTENT]... [COMMAND]

Commands:
  agents                 Manage external task executors end to end
  frameworks             Manage agent frameworks/engines end to end (LangGraph, CrewAI, …)
  start                  Ensure the global susi daemon is running and report host-contract endpoints
  stop                   Stop the global susi daemon (deterministic control plane — never a mission)
  restart                Restart the global susi daemon (stop then start — never a mission)
  install                Initialize sandboxed .susi environment
  install-release        Activate a qualified Windows release or restore the previous verified release
  local                  Build, test, integrate and qualify Susi locally through native guarded tools
  uninstall              Clean up sandboxed .susi environment
  mcp                    Manage leading MCP tool servers, or serve SUSI's native MCP stdio endpoint
  extensions             Manage extension packs (auto-seeded vendor opinions under ~/.susi/extensions) [alias: ext]
  auto                   Zero-config auto substrate: packs, MCP, models, peers readiness
  setup                  One end-to-end ecosystem setup: detect, consent, apply (safe to rerun)
  harness                Harness orchestration: author a plan, run a mission, serve the harness API
  tasks                  RSI eval-corpus runs (the task queue is `susi-commercial tasks`)
  brain                  The brain: which model susi trusts for which kind of work (evidence-ranked)
  ecosystem              Local AI ecosystem: installed engines/runtimes, GPU backends, explicit start [alias: eco]
  blackboard             Inspect the last mission blackboard (swarm shared state) [alias: bb]
  context-graph          Inspect and query the universal context graph [alias: cg]
  broker                 Inter-app permission and message broker
  telemetry              Sample host telemetry (thermal / battery / load)
  patch                  Apply a patch and run tests, rolling back on failure
  plan                   Solve a goal using the autonomous planning loop
  privacy                Privacy mode, egress consent, and cryptographic capability grants
  intent                 Semantic intent bus (advertise / need / match)
  ambient                Ambient FS → context graph / vector index sync
  tx                     Multi-agent transactional snapshots
  substrate              Pluggable / Sandbox / Governance / Host-contract / Reflexes status
  crown                  Tier S crown: verify every USP holds (Truth, Evidence, Swarm, …)
  gemi                   Start GEMI REST server
  status                 Inspect workspace health report
  services               Leaf-service process table: supervised pids, live health, restart
  commits                Audit the replicated quorum-commit ledger (signature-verified)
  os                     Operating-system view: consensus term/leader, services, verified peers
  peers                  Verified cluster roster: list peers, revoke a member's trust
  substrate-report       Report on autonomous invisible work performed by the substrate
  bloat-audit            Audit every Rust source in the workspace (AST-based, production code only) and target/ for bloat and hardcoded secrets, in parallel across all cores
  models                 Manage leading developer/agent models end to end
  openweight             Manage top open-weight frontier models end to end (Ollama/vLLM pull + prefer + probe) [alias: ow]
  frontier               Manage top frontier models end to end (Claude / GPT / DeepSeek / Gemini / Llama) [alias: fm]
  openrouter             Manage OpenRouter end to end (keys, prefer, probe, live models) [alias: or]
  keys                   Cloud API keys — list, set, prefer, remove (like `models` for backends) [alias: key]
  select-model           Select or override active model
  deep-scan              Parallel deep scan of substrate home for local models
  mcp-add                Open-admit an MCP server (stdio command or HTTP URL) into ~/.susi/mcp_config.json
  verify-download-agent  Verify model download agent, network status, and the hardware-selected model ladder
  scout-model            Scout or install model substrate via live foreground network stream
  benchmark              Measure real local inference latency/tokens-per-sec, and compare against a cloud endpoint if SUSI_BENCH_CLOUD_API_BASE is set
  pulse                  Ingest a natural language intent into sovereign memory (evidence.json)
  automate               First-class automation: run an autonomous evidence-gated swarm mission
  review                 Review daemon and OS environment status
  os-clean               Remove SUSI-owned residue (never host or other apps' caches) and report bytes freed
  audit                  Perform compliance audit and verify the tamper-evident audit chain
  admin                  Administrative commands
  clean                  Clean workspace build artifacts
  run                    Direct streaming model execution (local Ollama/llama.cpp/Candle or cloud)
  top                    Unified operator control surface: workload, resources, providers, config, federation, and evidence
  daemon-start           Internal daemon start (always binds to substrate home; --workspace kept for compat)
  help                   Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Arguments:
  [INTENT]...  Natural language intent or pulse

Options:
  -h, --help     Print help
  -V, --version  Print version

=== susi agents ===
Manage external task executors end to end

Usage: susi agents <COMMAND>

Commands:
  list       Show curated executors, native adapters, and installation documentation
  doctor     Check local prerequisites (does not invoke a paid model)
  setup      Show setup instructions and the effective adapter configuration
  configure  Load an adapter JSON file into trusted host configuration
  reset      Remove a host override and restore the bundled adapter
  run        Start a task; defaults to a detached worker with durable output
  tasks      List durable tasks in the current workspace
  status     Inspect a task; --refresh queries a cloud provider after worker loss/completion
  logs       Read the end of the task's captured output
  cancel     Request cancellation; cloud tasks are stopped through their native API
  send       Send a follow-up to an existing cloud task; then use status --refresh
  retry      Run a new task with the original prompt (does not resume the vendor session)
  help       Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi agents list ===
Show curated executors, native adapters, and installation documentation

Usage: susi agents list

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Arguments:
  [AGENT]

  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi agents run ===
Start a task; defaults to a detached worker with durable output

Usage: susi agents run [OPTIONS] <AGENT> <PROMPT>

Arguments:
  <AGENT>   
  <PROMPT>  Task prompt, passed as a single argv value, never evaluated by a shell

Options:
      --wait  Wait for the task to finish in this process
  -h, --help  Print help

  -h, --help  Print help

Arguments:
  <TASK_ID>  

Options:
      --refresh  
  -h, --help     Print help

=== susi agents logs ===

Arguments:
  <TASK_ID>  

Options:
      --stderr         
      --bytes <BYTES>  [default: 65536]
  -h, --help           Print help

  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi install-release ===
Activate a qualified Windows release or restore the previous verified release

Usage: susi install-release [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --id <ID>              Trusted SHA-256 release ID supplied by the local production qualifier
      --previous <PREVIOUS>  Qualified predecessor in the adjacent sibling release directory
      --rollback             Restore the previously admitted release
      --status               Verify the installed selector, executable, PATH and Start Menu entry
      --expect <EXPECT>      Require this specific release for verification or rollback
  -h, --help                 Print help

=== susi mcp ===
Manage leading MCP tool servers, or serve SUSI's native MCP stdio endpoint

Usage: susi mcp [COMMAND]

Commands:
  serve      Run SUSI's native MCP stdio server (default when bare `susi mcp`)
  list       Show the top MCP tool servers and enablement/readiness
  doctor     Check launchers and required env vars (does not start servers)
  setup      Show setup instructions and the effective adapter
  enable     Write the leading MCP into ~/.susi/mcp_config.json
  disable    Remove a leading MCP from ~/.susi/mcp_config.json
  configure  Override runner/args/env_keys/package via JSON file
  reset      Remove a host override and restore the bundled leading MCP entry
  status     Show enablement status for the top MCP servers
  ledger     Verify the pinned GMCP normative requirements ledger (.agents/gmcp): vendored corpus hashes, verbatim clauses, and complete row classification — the shipped production path for VC-203-001. `--drift` instead refetches every pinned upstream and fails closed on a changed or unreachable source
  call       Invoke a tool on a peer MCP endpoint (`host:port`) over the session-aware channel — the same path cluster replication uses
  tools      List the tools a peer MCP endpoint exposes (`tools/list` over the session-aware channel) — discover the surface before `mcp call`
  help       Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi mcp serve ===
Run SUSI's native MCP stdio server (default when bare `susi mcp`)

Usage: susi mcp serve

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi mcp ledger ===
Verify the pinned GMCP normative requirements ledger (.agents/gmcp): vendored corpus hashes, verbatim clauses, and complete row classification — the shipped production path for VC-203-001. `--drift` instead refetches every pinned upstream and fails closed on a changed or unreachable source

Usage: susi mcp ledger [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --drift                  Check upstream standards drift instead of the local corpus
      --refetched <REFETCHED>  With `--drift`: compare this pre-fetched corpus directory (keyed by manifest document name) instead of the network — the deterministic path tests and air-gapped checks use
  -h, --help                   Print help

=== susi mcp call ===
Invoke a tool on a peer MCP endpoint (`host:port`) over the session-aware channel — the same path cluster replication uses

Usage: susi mcp call [OPTIONS] <ADDR> <TOOL> [ARGS]

Arguments:
  <ADDR>  Peer address, e.g. 127.0.0.1:9093 (canonical GMCP-HTTP + port_offset)
  <TOOL>  Tool name as exposed by the peer's tools/list
  [ARGS]  JSON arguments object, e.g. '{"coordinator":"node-a"}' (default {}) [default: {}]

Options:
      --token <TOKEN>  Bearer token (default: cluster peer bearer for remote members, ~/.susi/api_token for loopback)
  -h, --help           Print help

=== susi mcp tools ===
List the tools a peer MCP endpoint exposes (`tools/list` over the session-aware channel) — discover the surface before `mcp call`

Usage: susi mcp tools [OPTIONS] <ADDR>

Arguments:
  <ADDR>  Peer address, e.g. 127.0.0.1:9093 (canonical GMCP-HTTP + port_offset)

Options:
      --token <TOKEN>  Bearer token (default: cluster peer bearer for remote members, ~/.susi/api_token for loopback)
  -h, --help           Print help

  status    Show active pack and substrate root
  create    Create an empty pack shell under ~/.susi/extensions/<id>/
  load      Load (activate) a pack
  unload    Unload a pack (keeps files; falls back to compiled defaults)
  validate  Check a pack directory against the host's admission rules (for pack authors; reads and changes no host state)
  help      Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi auto ===
Zero-config auto substrate: packs, MCP, models, peers readiness

Usage: susi auto [COMMAND]

Commands:
  status  Show zero-config auto substrate readiness (default). A snapshot of what the last prime wrote: the full report is refreshed only by `auto prime` and commands that prime every catalog (missions, in-process `mcp call`); the daemon and other commands prime only what they read, and the daemon never probes agent frameworks
  prime   Re-run auto-prime now (models/installed peers; never enables MCP)
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi auto status ===
Show zero-config auto substrate readiness (default). A snapshot of what the last prime wrote: the full report is refreshed only by `auto prime` and commands that prime every catalog (missions, in-process `mcp call`); the daemon and other commands prime only what they read, and the daemon never probes agent frameworks

Usage: susi auto status

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi auto prime ===
Re-run auto-prime now (models/installed peers; never enables MCP)

Usage: susi auto prime

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi setup ===
One end-to-end ecosystem setup: detect, consent, apply (safe to rerun)

Usage: susi setup [COMMAND]

Commands:
  plan   Detect hardware/engines/keys/agents and print the plan (default)
  apply  Apply the plan (optionally grant cloud consent)
  help   Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi setup plan ===
Detect hardware/engines/keys/agents and print the plan (default)

Usage: susi setup plan [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --json  Machine-readable plan for automation
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi setup apply ===
Apply the plan (optionally grant cloud consent)

Usage: susi setup apply [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --cloud  Grant cloud API key consent in this apply
      --json   Machine-readable result for automation
  -h, --help   Print help

=== susi harness ===
Harness orchestration: author a plan, run a mission, serve the harness API

Usage: susi harness <COMMAND>

Commands:
  author     Author a plan from a roadmap vector, through the metered gateway
  plan       Plan a batch of dependency-ready queue tasks; each entry claims its id
  run        Run a plan: prepare in parallel, land in order, persist after each task
  scorecard  Print the self-build (RSI) scorecard for the mission lifecycle ledger
  api        Serve the harness JSON/SSE API: spend, tasks, workers, warnings and operator commands
  status     Print the harness API snapshot for a ledger
  models     Print the provider registry, models and aliases as JSON (no network)
  budget     Print the one-line budget report and any top-up alert, without running
  gateway    Serve the metered multi-provider gateway directly from susi
  help       Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi harness author ===
Author a plan from a roadmap vector, through the metered gateway

Usage: susi harness author [OPTIONS] --gateway <GATEWAY> <VECTOR>

Arguments:
  <VECTOR>  Vector id, e.g. VC-203-001

Options:
      --gateway <GATEWAY>      Gateway base URL (the harness gateway)
      --model <MODEL>          Model id the gateway prices (such as `deepseek-pro`) [default: auto]
      --roadmap <ROADMAP>      Roadmap file [default: .agents/roadmap.json]
      --out <OUT>              Where to write the plan [default: plan.json]
      --max-tasks <MAX_TASKS>  Upper bound on tasks [default: 3]
      --workers <WORKERS>      Worker models tasks are spread across (comma-separated) [default: auto]
  -h, --help                   Print help

=== susi harness plan ===
Plan a batch of dependency-ready queue tasks; each entry claims its id

Usage: susi harness plan [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --repo <REPO>        The susi target repository [default: .]
      --out <OUT>          Where to write the plan [default: plan.json]
      --mission <MISSION>  Mission id [default: roadmap-batch]
      --limit <LIMIT>      Upper bound on tasks in the batch [default: 1]
      --workers <WORKERS>  Worker models, assigned round-robin (comma-separated) [default: auto]
      --roadmap <ROADMAP>  Only tasks whose roadmap vector is this id
      --gateway <GATEWAY>  Gateway the plan will run through: a listed worker whose provider has no key set here stays when that gateway answers for it (an explicit --upstream, or a gateway with its own key)
  -h, --help               Print help

=== susi harness run ===
Run a plan: prepare in parallel, land in order, persist after each task

Usage: susi harness run [OPTIONS] --gateway <GATEWAY> <PLAN>

Arguments:
  <PLAN>  Plan file

Options:
      --repo <REPO>                    The susi target repository [default: .]
      --state <STATE>                  Supervisor resume state [default: supervisor-state.json]
      --gateway <GATEWAY>              Gateway base URL (the harness gateway)
      --model <MODEL>                  Model id the gateway prices [default: auto]
      --timeout <TIMEOUT>              Per-turn deadline, seconds [default: 900]
      --parallel <PARALLEL>            Tasks prepared at once (landing is always serial) [default: 1]
      --prefix <PREFIX>                Worktree name prefix [default: harness]
      --workers <WORKERS>              Models a task may escalate to when its own model does not pass (comma-separated) [default: auto]
      --budget-usd <BUDGET_USD>        Mission cap in dollars [default: 5]
      --catalogue <CATALOGUE>          Price catalogue used to rank workers and bound spend [default: deploy/harness/prices.json]
      --daily-usd <DAILY_USD>          Daily spend ceiling in dollars, checked against the ledger before a run [default: 25]
      --ledger <LEDGER>                Ledger the gateway writes (spend authority) (default: `SUSI_HARNESS_LEDGER` if set, else `out/ledger.jsonl` in a susi workspace, else `harness/ledger.jsonl` in the data home, `~/.susi` unless `SUSI_HOME` is set; the same default standalone `susi-harness` uses)
      --controls <CONTROLS>            Control log the harness API writes pause/resume/abort to [default: out/control.jsonl]
      --rsi-log <RSI_LOG>              Self-build lifecycle ledger the RSI scorecard reads [default: .agents/rsi-loop.jsonl]
      --attempts <ATTEMPTS>            Hard cap on attempts per task [default: 3]
      --adapter-state <ADAPTER_STATE>  Where the adapter keeps prompts and results [default: harness-state]
      --susi <SUSI>                    The susi binary the adapter drives (default: this one)
  -h, --help                           Print help

=== susi harness scorecard ===
Print the self-build (RSI) scorecard for the mission lifecycle ledger

Usage: susi harness scorecard [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --events <EVENTS>   Lifecycle ledger the supervisor writes [default: .agents/rsi-loop.jsonl]
      --task <TASK>       Limit the report to one task (repeatable)
      --json              Machine-readable report
      --require-complete  Fail unless every task reached every phase
      --python <PYTHON>   Python executable [default: python]
  -h, --help              Print help

=== susi harness api ===
Serve the harness JSON/SSE API: spend, tasks, workers, warnings and operator commands

Usage: susi harness api [OPTIONS] --ledger <LEDGER>

Options:
      --ledger <LEDGER>          Ledger the gateway writes
      --events <EVENTS>          Event feed (default: beside the ledger)
      --state <STATE>            Supervisor resume state to show task progress
      --plan <PLAN>              Plan the supervisor is running
      --controls <CONTROLS>      Control log the operator's commands are appended to
      --catalogue <CATALOGUE>    Price catalogue, so each worker's rate is shown
      --graph <GRAPH>            Agent-graph bus file (overrides SUSI_HARNESS_GRAPH and the graph.jsonl beside the ledger)
      --budget-usd <BUDGET_USD>  Mission cap in dollars
      --mission <MISSION>        Mission to focus
      --host <HOST>              Interface to bind [default: 127.0.0.1]
      --port <PORT>              Port to bind [default: 9181]
  -h, --help                     Print help

Options:
      --ledger <LEDGER>  Ledger the gateway wrote
      --events <EVENTS>  Event feed (optional)
  -h, --help             Print help

=== susi harness gateway ===
Serve the metered multi-provider gateway directly from susi

Usage: susi harness gateway [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --port <PORT>            Port to bind (default: 9180) [default: 9180]
      --host <HOST>            Interface to bind (default: 127.0.0.1). Any address other machines can reach needs --accounts with at least one account [default: 127.0.0.1]
      --catalogue <CATALOGUE>  Price catalogue [default: deploy/harness/prices.json]
      --ledger <LEDGER>        Ledger path (default: `SUSI_HARNESS_LEDGER` if set, else `out/ledger.jsonl` in a susi workspace, else `harness/ledger.jsonl` in the data home, `~/.susi` unless `SUSI_HOME` is set; the same default standalone `susi-harness` uses)
      --upstream <UPSTREAM>    Upstream URL or "direct" for multi-provider routing [default: direct]
      --timeout <TIMEOUT>      Upstream call timeout in seconds [default: 120]
      --accounts <ACCOUNTS>    Accounts file: every caller must present a bearer token naming one of its accounts (optional on loopback, required on any other host)
  -h, --help                   Print help

=== susi tasks eval-corpus ===
Load the versioned RSI corpus, judge one candidate run against its held-out suite, and durably record the contamination/promotion evidence (VC-201-001). `--input` is a JSON file shaped {"candidate":{"id","actual_output","expected_results"}, "candidate_can_write","training_access","memory_access"}

=== susi brain ===
The brain: which model susi trusts for which kind of work (evidence-ranked)

Usage: susi brain [COMMAND]

Commands:
  status    Show the evidence-ranked providers for every task class (default)
  budget    Set shared cloud spending and request limits
  classify  Show which task class a prompt is routed as
  explain   Explain the brain's routing decision for a prompt
  export    Export brain evidence bundle to portable JSON format
  import    Import and merge brain evidence bundle from a file
  matrix    Show the measured capability matrix: every model's success rate, latency and cost per verified outcome at each task class
  pareto    Show the 3D Pareto frontier, Wilson 95% lower confidence bounds, and Bayesian UCB1 exploration-exploitation indices across providers
  cache     Show the measured prompt-cache hit rate and the estimated saving cache-first context assembly has realised so far
  reset     Forget all recorded outcomes (new account, changed model lineup)
  bench     Run the fixed prompt set against a fake or configured engine; record evidence
  probe     Probe a registered provider with the fixed scout benchmark and record the verified outcomes as brain evidence
  help      Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi brain status ===
Show the evidence-ranked providers for every task class (default)

Usage: susi brain status [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --top <TOP>      Number of top ranked providers to show per class [default: 5]
      --class <CLASS>  Filter by specific task class (e.g. reflex, chat, code, reasoning, estate_ops)
      --json           Output raw JSON instead of human summary table
  -h, --help           Print help

      --allow-paid

          Budget dial setting: low, balanced, or max
      --max-spend-microusd <MAX_SPEND_MICROUSD>
          
      --max-tokens <MAX_TOKENS>
          
      --max-requests <MAX_REQUESTS>
          
      --max-parallel <MAX_PARALLEL>
          
      --new-window
          Explicitly start a new accounting window; unresolved calls forbid reset
  -h, --help
          Print help

=== susi broker ===

  request    Request a permission (opens a negotiation)
  negotiate  Resolve a pending permission request
  pending    List pending permission requests
  check      Check whether an identity holds a scope
  revoke     Revoke a permission scope from an identity
  list       List grants for an identity
  send       Send a message to another identity (requires dispatch grant)

  help       Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

  -h, --help  Print help

  -g, --grantee <GRANTEE>    
  -r, --resource <RESOURCE>  
  -a, --action <ACTION>      
  -t, --ttl-secs <TTL_SECS>  
  -h, --help                 Print help

=== susi services ===
Leaf-service process table: supervised pids, live health, restart

Usage: susi services [COMMAND]

Commands:
  status   Show every leaf service, its supervised pid, and live health (default)
  restart  Terminate a supervised service; the daemon respawns it on its next probe
  stop     Stop a supervised service and hold it down — the supervisor will not respawn it until `susi services start` clears the stop flag. Distinct from restart: the service stays dead by operator intent
  start    Clear an operator stop and let the supervisor bring the service up
  logs     Tail a supervised service's log file (the daemon redirects each spawned service's stderr to `substrate_home/logs/<name>.log`)
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi services status ===
Show every leaf service, its supervised pid, and live health (default)

Usage: susi services status [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --json  Emit machine-readable JSON — agent callers get the process table as data instead of parsing the table view
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi services restart ===
Terminate a supervised service; the daemon respawns it on its next probe

Usage: susi services restart <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>  Service name: susi-paths, susi-error, susi-config, susi-sandbox, susi-native

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi services stop ===
Stop a supervised service and hold it down — the supervisor will not respawn it until `susi services start` clears the stop flag. Distinct from restart: the service stays dead by operator intent

Usage: susi services stop <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>  Service name: susi-paths, susi-error, susi-config, susi-sandbox, susi-native

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi services start ===
Clear an operator stop and let the supervisor bring the service up

Usage: susi services start <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>  Service name: susi-paths, susi-error, susi-config, susi-sandbox, susi-native

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi services logs ===
Tail a supervised service's log file (the daemon redirects each spawned service's stderr to `substrate_home/logs/<name>.log`)

Usage: susi services logs [OPTIONS] <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>  Service name: susi-paths, susi-error, susi-config, susi-sandbox, susi-native

Options:
  -n, --lines <LINES>  Number of trailing lines to print [default: 50]
  -h, --help           Print help

=== susi commits ===
Audit the replicated quorum-commit ledger (signature-verified)

Usage: susi commits [COMMAND]

Commands:
  list     List commit records, newest first (default)
  show     Print the full record (including committed value) for an epoch prefix
  audit    Whole-ledger consistency check: signature failures, sequence gaps, equivocation, and commits from non-elected coordinators
  replay   Fold the ledger into the cluster's consensus view (term, leader, per-coordinator high-water marks) — the state machine is a pure function of the log
  sync     Proactively pull records this node is missing from verified peers — the receive-path repair only fires when a *push* arrives, so a node that was offline during replication needs this to catch up
  compact  Fold the ledger into a snapshot and move pre-snapshot records to commit_log.archive.jsonl — bounds the live file's growth (Raft's InstallSnapshot analog). Local storage management, not a consensus event: the compacted and uncompacted views of the same history are identical
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi commits list ===
List commit records, newest first (default)

Usage: susi commits list [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -n, --limit <LIMIT>              Maximum records to show [default: 20]
      --coordinator <COORDINATOR>  Only records from this coordinator
      --term <TERM>                Only records sealed under this consensus term
      --kind <KIND>                Only records of this kind (decision, member_add, member_remove, member_unban)
      --json                       Emit machine-readable JSON instead of the table — the form agents and scripts should consume
  -h, --help                       Print help

=== susi commits show ===
Print the full record (including committed value) for an epoch prefix

Usage: susi commits show [OPTIONS] <EPOCH>

Arguments:
  <EPOCH>  Epoch hex prefix, e.g. the first 12 chars shown by `susi commits`

Options:
      --json  Emit machine-readable JSON — verification results ride inside the object instead of trailing human lines
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi commits audit ===
Whole-ledger consistency check: signature failures, sequence gaps, equivocation, and commits from non-elected coordinators

Usage: susi commits audit [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --strict  Exit nonzero when anomalies are found — lets CI and operators gate on ledger health instead of eyeballing output
      --json    Emit machine-readable JSON — agents and CI get structured anomalies instead of parsing log lines
  -h, --help    Print help

=== susi commits replay ===
Fold the ledger into the cluster's consensus view (term, leader, per-coordinator high-water marks) — the state machine is a pure function of the log

Usage: susi commits replay [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --json  Emit machine-readable JSON — the consensus view as data
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi commits sync ===
Proactively pull records this node is missing from verified peers — the receive-path repair only fires when a *push* arrives, so a node that was offline during replication needs this to catch up

Usage: susi commits sync

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi commits compact ===
Fold the ledger into a snapshot and move pre-snapshot records to commit_log.archive.jsonl — bounds the live file's growth (Raft's InstallSnapshot analog). Local storage management, not a consensus event: the compacted and uncompacted views of the same history are identical

Usage: susi commits compact

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi os ===
Operating-system view: consensus term/leader, services, verified peers

Usage: susi os [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  status        Full substrate status: consensus, services, peers (default)
  clean         Remove stray heavyweight files flagged in `~/.susi/bin` and report reclaimed space
  ecosystem     Discover the local AI ecosystem: hardware, runtimes, models, agents, frameworks, MCP servers, and running AI processes
  runtime       Live runtime view: AI processes by owner (SUSI vs external), managed models with observed residency, and per-process GPU memory
  route         Explain the live local-versus-cloud inference placement decision
  route-reset   Re-admit a repaired cloud provider after routing quarantine
  manage        Unified lifecycle facade for local AI ecosystem components
  provision     Explicit cloud/local host provision. The 30s OS tick runs no operator CLI; probe/list/apply run only on request — that is the OS contract, not a silent cloud API
  capabilities  The unified capability bus: discover every A2A/MCP/HTTP/adapter capability through one typed catalog, or dispatch one through its permission/timeout/cost contract (Mcp tools only today)
  help          Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --json  Emit machine-readable JSON instead of the table view
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi os status ===
Full substrate status: consensus, services, peers (default)

Usage: susi os status [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --json  Emit machine-readable JSON instead of the table view
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi os clean ===
Remove stray heavyweight files flagged in `~/.susi/bin` and report reclaimed space

Usage: susi os clean

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi os ecosystem ===
Discover the local AI ecosystem: hardware, runtimes, models, agents, frameworks, MCP servers, and running AI processes

Usage: susi os ecosystem [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --json    Emit machine-readable JSON
      --doctor  Exit unsuccessfully when installed components are unhealthy
  -h, --help    Print help

=== susi os runtime ===
Live runtime view: AI processes by owner (SUSI vs external), managed models with observed residency, and per-process GPU memory

Usage: susi os runtime [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --json  Emit machine-readable JSON
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi os route ===
Explain the live local-versus-cloud inference placement decision

Usage: susi os route [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --json                 Emit machine-readable JSON
      --requires <REQUIRES>  Required model capability, for example `vision`
      --max-cost <MAX_COST>  Maximum acceptable request-cost hint in USD
      --no-cloud             Prohibit placement on cloud providers
  -h, --help                 Print help

=== susi os route-reset ===
Re-admit a repaired cloud provider after routing quarantine

Usage: susi os route-reset <PROVIDER>

Arguments:
  <PROVIDER>  Exact provider id shown by `susi os route --json`

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi os provision ===
Explicit cloud/local host provision. The 30s OS tick runs no operator CLI; probe/list/apply run only on request — that is the OS contract, not a silent cloud API

Usage: susi os provision <COMMAND>

Commands:
  probe  PATH version-probe of kubectl/docker/aws/gcloud/az (on request only)
  list   Live inventory (`kubectl get nodes`, `docker ps`, cloud instance list)
  apply  Apply a Kubernetes manifest (`kubectl apply -f`). Other kinds refuse
  help   Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi os provision probe ===
PATH version-probe of kubectl/docker/aws/gcloud/az (on request only)

Usage: susi os provision probe [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --json  
  -h, --help  Print help

Live inventory (`kubectl get nodes`, `docker ps`, cloud instance list)

Usage: susi os provision list [OPTIONS] <KIND>

Arguments:
  <KIND>  kubernetes|docker|aws|gcp|azure

Options:
      --json  
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi os provision apply ===
Apply a Kubernetes manifest (`kubectl apply -f`). Other kinds refuse

Usage: susi os provision apply <KIND> <MANIFEST>

Arguments:
  <KIND>      kubernetes (kubectl-only)
  <MANIFEST>  Manifest file path

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi os capabilities ===
The unified capability bus: discover every A2A/MCP/HTTP/adapter capability through one typed catalog, or dispatch one through its permission/timeout/cost contract (Mcp tools only today)

Usage: susi os capabilities [COMMAND]

Commands:
  discover  List every discovered capability (default)
  invoke    Dispatch one capability through its permission/timeout/cost contract
  delegate  Issue a host-signed delegation envelope: `subject` may exercise `id` with `permission`, budget and timeout, nested under `--delegation` (or a fresh root for `subject`) and never beyond it
  help      Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi os capabilities discover ===
List every discovered capability (default)

Usage: susi os capabilities discover [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --json  
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi os capabilities invoke ===
Dispatch one capability through its permission/timeout/cost contract

Usage: susi os capabilities invoke [OPTIONS] --permission <PERMISSION> <ID>

Arguments:
  <ID>  Capability id to dispatch (as shown by discover)

Options:
      --subject <SUBJECT>              Subject credited/audited for the invocation [default: operator]
      --permission <PERMISSION>        Permission held by the subject, e.g. `capability:tool`
      --args <ARGS>                    JSON args passed to the invoked tool [default: {}]
      --timeout-ms <TIMEOUT_MS>        [default: 30000]
      --budget-micros <BUDGET_MICROS>  [default: 18446744073709551615]
      --delegation <DELEGATION>        Host-signed `susi-delegation/v1` envelope (JSON) from the calling driver: the call nests under it and cannot exceed it
      --json                           
  -h, --help                           Print help

=== susi os capabilities delegate ===
Issue a host-signed delegation envelope: `subject` may exercise `id` with `permission`, budget and timeout, nested under `--delegation` (or a fresh root for `subject`) and never beyond it

Usage: susi os capabilities delegate [OPTIONS] --permission <PERMISSION> <ID>

Arguments:
  <ID>  Capability (or role) the subject will exercise

Options:
      --subject <SUBJECT>              Component the envelope is issued to [default: operator]
      --permission <PERMISSION>        Permission the subject may present
      --timeout-ms <TIMEOUT_MS>        [default: 30000]
      --budget-micros <BUDGET_MICROS>  [default: 18446744073709551615]
      --delegation <DELEGATION>        Parent host-signed envelope (JSON); absent opens a fresh root
  -h, --help                           Print help

=== susi peers ===
Verified cluster roster: list peers, revoke a member's trust

Usage: susi peers [COMMAND]

Commands:
  list    List verified peers and banned members (default)
  add     Bootstrap cluster membership: send a cluster-key-signed discovery ping to a host and persist the verified responder as an explicit member. Fails closed when the peer doesn't hold our cluster.key
  probe   Probe a peer without persisting anything: the same signed-ping → signed-pong handshake `peers add` performs, reporting only the responder's attested identity and its standing in this node's roster. The non-destructive way to test reachability and cluster.key compatibility before (or instead of) `peers add`
  remove  Evict a peer: revoke persisted trust AND ban re-verification. The ban is enforced at the signed-pong handshake — the peer cannot rejoin until `susi peers unban` lifts it
  unban   Lift a ban so a previously evicted peer can re-verify
  rekey   Rotate the cluster key across every verified member — the only way to truly revoke an evicted member's cluster.key. Two-phase: a `cluster_rekey` record commits WHICH key members stage; a `cluster_rekey_activate` record then triggers rotation. If any member fails to stage, the rotation aborts safely (nothing activates anywhere) unless `--force` is given. Members that don't acknowledge activation are cryptographically stranded
  status  Cluster-wide consensus view: call `cluster_status` on every rostered member (member-signed requests) and print each node's term, leader view, ledger size, and key epoch side by side — divergence shows up directly as differing terms, epochs, or record counts
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi peers list ===
List verified peers and banned members (default)

Usage: susi peers list [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --json  Emit machine-readable JSON instead of the table view
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi peers add ===
Bootstrap cluster membership: send a cluster-key-signed discovery ping to a host and persist the verified responder as an explicit member. Fails closed when the peer doesn't hold our cluster.key

Usage: susi peers add [OPTIONS] <HOST>

Arguments:
  <HOST>  IP or hostname of the peer daemon to join (may include :port)

Options:
      --port <PORT>  UDP discovery port (default: host-contract 9092 + port_offset)
  -h, --help         Print help

=== susi peers probe ===
Probe a peer without persisting anything: the same signed-ping → signed-pong handshake `peers add` performs, reporting only the responder's attested identity and its standing in this node's roster. The non-destructive way to test reachability and cluster.key compatibility before (or instead of) `peers add`

Usage: susi peers probe [OPTIONS] <HOST>

Arguments:
  <HOST>  IP or hostname of the peer daemon to probe (may include :port)

Options:
      --port <PORT>  UDP discovery port (default: host-contract 9092 + port_offset)
  -h, --help         Print help

=== susi peers remove ===
Evict a peer: revoke persisted trust AND ban re-verification. The ban is enforced at the signed-pong handshake — the peer cannot rejoin until `susi peers unban` lifts it

Usage: susi peers remove <PEER>

Arguments:
  <PEER>  node_id or address prefix of the peer to evict

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi peers unban ===
Lift a ban so a previously evicted peer can re-verify

Usage: susi peers unban <PEER>

Arguments:
  <PEER>  node_id or address of the banned peer to restore

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi peers rekey ===
Rotate the cluster key across every verified member — the only way to truly revoke an evicted member's cluster.key. Two-phase: a `cluster_rekey` record commits WHICH key members stage; a `cluster_rekey_activate` record then triggers rotation. If any member fails to stage, the rotation aborts safely (nothing activates anywhere) unless `--force` is given. Members that don't acknowledge activation are cryptographically stranded

Usage: susi peers rekey [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --force  Proceed to activation even when some members failed to stage — those members will be stranded and must be re-provisioned with the new key manually
  -h, --help   Print help

=== susi peers status ===
Cluster-wide consensus view: call `cluster_status` on every rostered member (member-signed requests) and print each node's term, leader view, ledger size, and key epoch side by side — divergence shows up directly as differing terms, epochs, or record counts

Usage: susi peers status [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --json  Emit machine-readable JSON instead of the table view
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi service-run ===
Run one leaf service in-process — the daemon's spawn mode: the staged `susi` binary re-execs itself as `service-run <name>` so supervised services need no sibling binaries on disk

Usage: susi service-run [OPTIONS] <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>  Leaf service name: susi-paths | susi-error | susi-config | susi-sandbox | susi-native

Options:
      --port <PORT>  Port override (defaults to the service's contract port env var)
  -h, --help         Print help

=== susi models ===
Manage leading developer/agent models end to end

Usage: susi models [COMMAND]

Commands:
  list       Show the top developer/agent-focused models and readiness
  doctor     Check credentials/endpoints (does not call a paid model)
  setup      Show setup instructions and the effective model wiring
  configure  Override engine/model/protocol/api_key_env via JSON file
  reset      Remove a host override and restore the bundled coding-model entry
  prefer     Prefer a coding model for subsequent routing (`selected_model_override`)
  probe      Paid probe: send a short completion to verify auth and model id
  help       Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi openweight ===
Manage top open-weight frontier models end to end (Ollama/vLLM pull + prefer + probe)

Usage: susi openweight [COMMAND]

Commands:
  list       Show the top open-weight frontier models and readiness
  doctor     Check local endpoint / pull status (does not download weights)
  setup      Show setup instructions and effective wiring
  pull       Pull weights via `ollama pull <tag>`
  configure  Override engine/ollama_tag/protocol via JSON file
  reset      Remove a host override and restore the bundled entry
  prefer     Prefer an open-weight model for local routing
  probe      Local probe: short completion via Ollama/vLLM
  help       Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi openweight list ===
Show the top open-weight frontier models and readiness

Usage: susi openweight list

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi openweight doctor ===
Check local endpoint / pull status (does not download weights)

Usage: susi openweight doctor [MODEL]

Arguments:
  [MODEL]  

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi openweight setup ===
Show setup instructions and effective wiring

Usage: susi openweight setup <MODEL>

Arguments:
  <MODEL>  

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi openweight pull ===
Pull weights via `ollama pull <tag>`

Usage: susi openweight pull <MODEL>

Arguments:
  <MODEL>  

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi openweight configure ===
Override engine/ollama_tag/protocol via JSON file

Usage: susi openweight configure <MODEL> <FILE>

Arguments:
  <MODEL>  
  <FILE>   

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

  <MODEL>

  -h, --help  Print help

Usage: susi openweight prefer [OPTIONS] [MODEL]

  [MODEL]  

Options:

  -h, --help   Print help

=== susi frontier ===
Manage top frontier models end to end (Claude / GPT / DeepSeek / Gemini / Llama)

Usage: susi frontier [COMMAND]

Commands:
  list       Show the top frontier models and readiness
  doctor     Check credentials/endpoints (does not call a paid model)
  setup      Show setup instructions and effective wiring
  configure  Override engine/model/protocol/api_key_env via JSON file
  reset      Remove a host override and restore the bundled entry
  prefer     Prefer a frontier model for subsequent routing
  probe      Probe: short completion via cloud or local endpoint
  help       Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi openrouter ===
Manage OpenRouter end to end (keys, prefer, probe, live models)

Usage: susi openrouter [COMMAND]

Commands:
  list    Show OpenRouter status and curated routes
  doctor  Check key + endpoint readiness (does not call a paid model unless --live)
  setup   Show setup instructions and effective wiring
  prefer  Prefer OpenRouter for cloud routing; optionally pin a model/route id
  probe   Paid probe: short completion via the effective OpenRouter model
  models  List curated routes, or live provider model ids with --live
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi openrouter list ===
Show OpenRouter status and curated routes

Usage: susi openrouter list

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi openrouter doctor ===
Check key + endpoint readiness (does not call a paid model unless --live)

Usage: susi openrouter doctor [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --live  Also hit GET /models to verify the key works
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi openrouter setup ===
Show setup instructions and effective wiring

Usage: susi openrouter setup

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi openrouter prefer ===
Prefer OpenRouter for cloud routing; optionally pin a model/route id

Usage: susi openrouter prefer [OPTIONS] [MODEL]

Arguments:
  [MODEL]  Catalog id (e.g. claude-sonnet) or raw OpenRouter model slug

Options:
      --clear-model  Clear the pinned model (keep cloud preference)
  -h, --help         Print help

=== susi openrouter probe ===
Paid probe: short completion via the effective OpenRouter model

Usage: susi openrouter probe [PROMPT]

Arguments:
  [PROMPT]  [default: "Reply with exactly: ok"]

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi openrouter models ===
List curated routes, or live provider model ids with --live

Usage: susi openrouter models [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --live           
      --limit <LIMIT>  [default: 50]
  -h, --help           Print help

=== susi keys ===
Cloud API keys — list, set, prefer, remove (like `models` for backends)

Usage: susi keys [COMMAND]

Commands:
  set     Save a vendor API key and register the cloud provider
  list    Show which known vendors have a key configured (never prints secrets)
  prefer  Prefer a cloud vendor when several keys are registered (e.g. paid over free)
  remove  Remove a vendor API key from ~/.susi/cloud.env
  check   Live-check registered keys against each vendor (one read-only /models call each)
  models  List the models a vendor serves right now (uses the registered key)
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi keys set ===
Save a vendor API key and register the cloud provider

Usage: susi keys set <VENDOR> [API_KEY]

Arguments:
  <VENDOR>   Vendor: openai, anthropic, gemini, deepseek, kimi, minimax, openrouter, …
  [API_KEY]  API key (omit to be prompted, or pipe via stdin)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi keys list ===
Show which known vendors have a key configured (never prints secrets)

Usage: susi keys list

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi keys prefer ===
Prefer a cloud vendor when several keys are registered (e.g. paid over free)

Usage: susi keys prefer [OPTIONS] [VENDOR]

Arguments:
  [VENDOR]  Vendor to prefer (openai, deepseek, …). Omit to show current preference

Options:
      --clear  Clear the sticky preferred cloud
  -h, --help   Print help

=== susi keys remove ===
Remove a vendor API key from ~/.susi/cloud.env

Usage: susi keys remove <VENDOR>

Arguments:
  <VENDOR>  

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi keys check ===
Live-check registered keys against each vendor (one read-only /models call each)

Usage: susi keys check [VENDOR]

Arguments:
  [VENDOR]  Vendor or alias (e.g. xai, grok, together). Omit to check every cloud vendor

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi keys models ===
List the models a vendor serves right now (uses the registered key)

Usage: susi keys models <VENDOR>

Arguments:
  <VENDOR>  Vendor or alias (e.g. fireworks, deepinfra)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi mcp-add ===
Open-admit an MCP server (stdio command or HTTP URL) into ~/.susi/mcp_config.json

Usage: susi mcp-add <NAME> <COMMAND_OR_URL> [ARGS]...

Arguments:
  <NAME>            Registry name for the server
  <COMMAND_OR_URL>  Stdio command or streamable HTTP MCP URL (`http://…` / `https://…`)
  [ARGS]...         Extra argv for stdio MCP servers

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi audit ===
Perform compliance audit and verify the tamper-evident audit chain

Usage: susi audit [COMMAND]

Commands:
  verify  Verify every audit record, optionally reporting entries since a Unix timestamp
  query   Query redacted action history by actor, mission, kind, and time
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi audit verify ===
Verify every audit record, optionally reporting entries since a Unix timestamp

Usage: susi audit verify [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --since <SINCE>  Only count verified entries at or after this Unix timestamp; the full chain is checked
  -h, --help           Print help

=== susi audit query ===
Query redacted action history by actor, mission, kind, and time

Usage: susi audit query [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --actor <ACTOR>      
      --mission <MISSION>  
      --kind <KIND>        
      --since <SINCE>      
      --until <UNTIL>      
      --json               Emit the query result as a JSON array
  -h, --help               Print help

=== susi admin ===
Administrative commands

Usage: susi admin <COMMAND>

Commands:
  pulse              Ingest pulse via admin
  audit              Compliance audit
  audit-evidence     Export and independently verify redacted audit evidence [alias: evidence]
  lint               Run clippy
  audit-deps         Run cargo audit
  reload             Dynamic configuration hot-reload
  provider-contract  Provider contract checks: fixture-backed checks always; credentialed live probes when SUSI_PROVIDER_PROBE=1
  intent-ladder      The graded user-intent ladder: print the last scorecard (default), run the full ladder hermetically (--run), or just the bounded start-up slice (--slice). The daemon records failing rungs in the host outbox (--gaps); an agent adopts one as a repair task in its own checkout with `susi-commercial admin intent-ladder --adopt-gap`
  help               Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi admin pulse ===
Ingest pulse via admin

Usage: susi admin pulse [INTENT]...

Arguments:
  [INTENT]...  

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi admin audit ===
Compliance audit

Usage: susi admin audit

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi admin audit-evidence ===
Export and independently verify redacted audit evidence

Usage: susi admin audit-evidence <COMMAND>

Commands:
  export  Wrap a JSON segment list in the stable file format
  verify  Verify a file against one or more key-id=secret pairs
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi admin audit-evidence export ===
Wrap a JSON segment list in the stable file format

Usage: susi admin audit-evidence export --input <FILE> --output <FILE>

Options:
      --input <FILE>   JSON array of redacted audit segments (or an existing export)
      --output <FILE>  Destination for the independently verifiable export
  -h, --help           Print help

=== susi admin audit-evidence verify ===
Verify a file against one or more key-id=secret pairs

Usage: susi admin audit-evidence verify [OPTIONS] --input <FILE>

Options:
      --input <FILE>      Export file to verify [alias: --file]
      --key <KEY=SECRET>  Signing key in key-id=secret form; repeat for multiple keys [alias: --keys]
  -h, --help              Print help

=== susi admin intent-ladder ===
The graded user-intent ladder: print the last scorecard (default), run the full ladder hermetically (--run), or just the bounded start-up slice (--slice). The daemon records failing rungs in the host outbox (--gaps); an agent adopts one as a repair task in its own checkout with `susi-commercial admin intent-ladder --adopt-gap`

Usage: susi admin intent-ladder [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --run          Run every rung now — hermetic, wall-clock bounded
      --slice        Run only the start-up slice
      --verify <ID>  Re-check one intent id hermetically — the acceptance a repair task's close runs; exits nonzero unless the intent passes
      --gaps         Print the host outbox of failing rungs (`<home>/intent-gaps.json`)
  -h, --help         Print help

=== susi clean ===
Clean workspace build artifacts

Usage: susi clean

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

=== susi run ===
Direct streaming model execution (local Ollama/llama.cpp/Candle or cloud)

Usage: susi run [OPTIONS] [PROMPT]...

Arguments:
  [PROMPT]...  Positional model name and/or prompt tokens

Options:
  -m, --model <MODEL>    Model name (e.g. `qwen2.5-coder:7b`, `claude-3-7-sonnet`, `deepseek-chat`)
  -s, --system <SYSTEM>  System prompt / instructions
      --no-stream        Disable streaming output (buffers complete response before printing)
      --json             Output JSON with metadata (duration, token throughput, serving backend)
  -h, --help             Print help

=== susi top ===
Unified operator control surface: workload, resources, providers, config, federation, and evidence

Usage: susi top [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --json             Output the operator control surface state as JSON
      --filter <FILTER>  Filter to a specific state dimension: workload, resources, providers, config, federation, evidence
  -h, --help             Print help

=== susi daemon-start ===
Internal daemon start (always binds to substrate home; --workspace kept for compat)

Usage: susi daemon-start [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  [default: ""]
  -h, --help                   Print help
